<ol class="learning-cycle" aria-label="Four connected research questions">
<li class="cycle-stage"><article><span class="theme-number">01</span><p class="cycle-role">Existing knowledge and its relevance across places.</p><h3><a href="/research/geographies-of-climate-learning.html">Geographies of Climate Learning</a></h3><p class="guiding-question">How does place shape which urban climate knowledge is produced, recognised and useful elsewhere?</p><p>We study how urban climate knowledge is distributed across places, which cities can plausibly learn from one another, and how institutional and geographic context shapes the relevance of evidence produced elsewhere.</p><p><a class="text-link" href="/research/geographies-of-climate-learning.html">Explore this question <span aria-hidden="true">→</span></a></p></article></li>
<li class="cycle-stage"><article><span class="theme-number">02</span><span class="theme-status developing">Developing</span><p class="cycle-role">Choices about which uncertainties and evidence gaps merit investigation.</p><h3><a href="/research/where-new-evidence-matters.html">Where New Evidence Matters</a></h3><p class="guiding-question">Which new evidence would most improve urban climate decisions?</p><p>We develop approaches for identifying where new cases, evaluations, datasets and forms of knowledge could resolve consequential uncertainty or expand the learning options available to cities.</p><p><a class="text-link" href="/research/where-new-evidence-matters.html">Explore this question <span aria-hidden="true">→</span></a></p></article></li>
<li class="cycle-stage"><article><span class="theme-number">03</span><p class="cycle-role">The arrangements through which climate action becomes operable.</p><h3><a href="/research/modes-of-climate-delivery.html">Modes of Climate Delivery</a></h3><p class="guiding-question">Through which institutional arrangements does urban climate action become possible and durable?</p><p>We examine how climate action is authorised, financed, coordinated, implemented and maintained, and why similar interventions depend on different delivery configurations in different places.</p><p><a class="text-link" href="/research/modes-of-climate-delivery.html">Explore this question <span aria-hidden="true">→</span></a></p></article></li>
<li class="cycle-stage"><article><span class="theme-number">04</span><p class="cycle-role">Observed outcomes, their distribution, and evidence that informs subsequent decisions.</p><h3><a href="/research/consequences-for-people-and-places.html">Consequences for People and Places</a></h3><p class="guiding-question">What does climate action change, for whom, where and over what period?</p><p>We study how climate action affects health, equity, social cohesion and other dimensions of wellbeing, including how benefits, burdens and risks are distributed across populations and places.</p><p><a class="text-link" href="/research/consequences-for-people-and-places.html">Explore this question <span aria-hidden="true">→</span></a></p></article></li>
<li class="cycle-return"><strong>Consequences generate further learning.</strong> Outcomes, burdens and unresolved questions return to the first two stages as new evidence and revised judgements.</li></ol>
